title: Neuracle invasive brain-computer interface
summary: Wireless epidural implants that let paralysed patients control external devices.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Neuracle, working with Tsinghua University, implanted wireless epidural electrodes in patients with spinal cord injury and demonstrated control of cursor and robotic devices through decoded motor intent. The approach avoids penetrating the cortex, trading signal quality for safety. Trials remain small and long-term stability is unproven.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2023–2030
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

China is running invasive trials at a pace that may produce the first large clinical dataset outside the United States.

What Would Change The View

  • Cohort size and follow-up duration.
  • Decoder generalisation across patients.
  • Regulatory pathway for chronic implants.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
